/bin/bash -c "mkdir -p tmp/pdfs
python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
from pypdf import PdfReader
reader=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
print('Pages:', len(reader.pages))
for i,page in enumerate(reader.pages,1):
    text=page.extract_text(extraction_mode='layout')
    Path(f'tmp/pdfs/page-{i:02}.txt').write_text(text)
    print(f'Page {i}: {len(text)} characters')
Path('tmp/pdfs/manuscript.txt').write_text('\\n\\n'.join(f'===== PAGE {i+1} =====\\n'+p.read_text() for i,p in enumerate(sorted(Path('tmp/pdfs').glob('page-*.txt')))))
print(reader.metadata)
PY"

strengths: The method addresses a relevant computer vision problem and demonstrates practical gains at ImageNet-1K scale. Against replicated SRe2L, accuracy improves from 54.4% to 57.6% at 50 images per class and from 58.3% to 60.7% at 100 images per class.

Evaluation includes three datasets, multiple compression budgets, repeated runs, architecture transfer, component ablations, and regularization sensitivity. Reporting both published and substantially improved replicated SRe2L results strengthens the comparison.

Class-specific BatchNorm matching is an empirically useful component. The manuscript explicitly credits SRe2L, DeepInversion, the established barycenter algorithms, and POT, and supplies pseudocode and recovery hyperparameters.
weaknesses: The central contribution is insufficiently distinguished from standard feature quantization. With squared Euclidean cost and freely optimized probability masses, the unregularized objective in Eq. (4) reduces to k-means quantization of the empirical distribution. The paper neither explains this connection nor compares against k-means feature targets. A matched MMD experiment using the same teacher, regularization, and relabeling is also missing, leaving the claimed advantage of Wasserstein geometry inadequately established.

The weighted formulation is not connected clearly to the final training procedure. Equations (3)–(4) and the appendix optimize nonuniform support masses, but Algorithm 1 outputs only synthetic images, and Eq. (5) matches support locations without explaining how the masses enter sampling or classifier training. Thus, correspondence between the optimized distribution and the distribution actually used for training remains unresolved.

Table III attributes most of the improvement to class-specific BatchNorm statistics. With cross-entropy and class-specific BatchNorm held fixed, adding the barycenter loss changes accuracy by only -0.1, +0.8, and +0.5 percentage points on ImageNette, Tiny ImageNet, and ImageNet-1K, respectively. These results support a useful refinement but provide limited evidence for the paper's emphasis on Wasserstein matching. Component ablations at larger image budgets are absent.

The core transport computation is incompletely specified. Section III-B describes entropic regularization, while the appendix presents unregularized transport linear programs and does not specify an entropy coefficient, concrete initialization, or convergence tolerances. This ambiguity affects reproducibility of the feature targets and computational cost.

The efficiency claim lacks adequate comparative evidence. Table IV reports only a synthetic-image update on 64×64 ImageNette, without baseline timings or an accounting of feature extraction, transport computation, and relabeling. The supplementary 14-hour ImageNet experiment does not establish an end-to-end efficiency advantage.

The broader generalization and diversity claims exceed the evidence. Table II lacks transfer comparisons against competing distilled datasets and shows weak ViT performance. Figure 4 uses representations trained on mixtures containing the synthetic data being evaluated, so its t-SNE plots provide limited independent evidence of improved distribution coverage or reduced reliance on background shortcuts.
